entities.name: PMID:27519527
observations: 2016 meta-analysis included 5 randomized and 6 clinical controlled trials (1,240 patients). Perioperative versus adjuvant chemotherapy improved overall survival: HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.61–0.89. Combination neoadjuvant regimens benefited, whereas fluoropyrimidine monotherapy did not. Postoperative complications and chemotherapy adverse effects were not significantly different.

entities.name: PMID:26242393
observations: 2015 updated meta-analysis of randomized trials found no significant overall-survival benefit for neoadjuvant-containing strategies overall, but perioperative treatment with both neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemotherapy versus adjuvant chemotherapy alone improved OS: HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.35–0.67. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone did not improve survival over surgery alone.

entities.name: PMID:37532103
observations: 2024 systematic review/meta-analysis included 18 studies and 4,686 patients. Perioperative versus adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved OS (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.69–0.87) and DFS (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.69–0.84), with higher R0 resection and similar postoperative complication/adverse-event rates. Authors emphasized Asian resectable-gastric-cancer populations.

entities.name: PMID:40115020
observations: 2025 RCT-only meta-analysis included 5 randomized trials and 2,735 patients. Neoadjuvant/perioperative chemotherapy improved PFS versus adjuvant chemotherapy: HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.69–0.85. OS favored neoadjuvant treatment numerically but was not statistically significant: HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.70–1.07; OS sensitivity analysis was unstable. PFS benefit was clearest in women and clinically node-positive patients.

entities.name: PMID:30217320
observations: 2018 Bayesian network meta-analysis of 33 randomized trials found perioperative chemotherapy had the highest probability of being best, but there was no statistically significant OS difference between perioperative chemotherapy and postoperative chemotherapy. Compared with surgery alone, perioperative chemotherapy improved OS: HR 0.69, 95% credible interval 0.55–0.84.
